section_summary.extract_value: This abstract describes a single study examining the buffering role of self-compassion on the relationship between interactions with body-focused others and eating/body image outcomes. The study involved 92 female undergraduates who reported daily for seven nights on social interactions, self-compassion, body image, eating, and affect. Results indicate that self-compassion moderated the negative effects of body-focused social interactions on body image concerns and body appreciation.
